_README: Active demotions list.  Each entry skips bet placement on STRONG
rows whose features match the predicate.  Operator adds entries
ONLY after a candidate cluster from cluster_discovery.py is
confirmed by the loss_cluster_monitor.py Telegram alert (i.e.
the cluster's recent-N record has actually crossed the bad-
performance threshold, not just looked bad in one batch).
What demotion does: rewrites the row to render as PASS (pick_side
and pick_strength become 'PASS' / 'NO EDGE', pick_label encodes the
original verdict + cluster id, bet_placed='N' + units_risked='').
The dashboard surfaces the demotion via a tooltip on the PASS pill.
Reversible: flip 'active' to false (or remove the entry) and the
next predict cron lets future bets in the cluster auto-commit.
Format: each entry under 'demotions' has:
id            stable identifier (used in pick_changes journal)
reason        human-readable why
side          'NRFI' | 'YRFI' | null (null = either side)
nrfi_prob     {min, max} -- both inclusive; null skips bound
combined_lambda {min, max} -- optional
park_factor   {min, max} -- optional
pitcher_quality_min  list of {sm,ltd,live,avg} the worst-quality
pitcher must be in (e.g., ['sm','ltd']);
null = any quality matches
active        bool; false = present but disabled
reevaluate_after  ISO date YYYY-MM-DD (optional).  On/after this
date, tools/demotion_reeval_reminder.py fires a
Telegram with the current shadow-P&L snapshot so
the operator can decide keep/flip/remove.
Apply with: python tools/apply_cluster_demotion.py

demotions.reason: RETIRED 2026-05-12.  Original evidence (6W-10L over 5 days, n=16) was small-sample noise.  Walk-forward backtest across the full 2026 season (tools/v23_walkforward_backtest.py) showed thin-pitcher STRONG bets generated +19u that this demotion would have skipped -- the 5-day losing streak was not representative.  Better fix for the underlying regime drift is a recent-form feature on top-3 batters (Phase G).  Original 5-day evidence: 6W-10L (-5.34u) over 5 days post-v2.1 deploy (5/06-5/10).
